messages.author: 71aafe226d17b79c
messages.subject: Joint survival-longitudinal model in stan
parts:
Hi all,
I am running a joint survival-longitudinal model in stan with a normal distribution for longitudinal part. I think my code is correct but the model does not provide reasonable output.
I have attached annotated code. Could you please take a look at the code and figure out what is going wrong? I tried using ljk-cholesky for correlation between coefficients but the result was disappointing.
Many Thanks.

data{
    
    int <lower=0> nsubj; //subject id (1360)
    int <lower=0> ntot; // total obs (3700)
    int <lower=1,upper=nsubj> subj [ntot]; //longitudinal subj id 
    int npredlong; // number of rpedictors in longitudinal part (here 4)
    int npredsurv; // number of rpedictors in survival part (here 3)
    int nraneff; //  number of random effects(hete 2)
    int<lower=0> nuncens; //  number of uncensored obs
    int<lower=0> ncens; // number of censored obs
    matrix [ntot,npredlong] xlong; // design matrix for longitudinal part
    matrix [nuncens,npredsurv] xuncens; // design matrix for uncensored obs
    matrix [ncens,npredsurv] xcens; // design matrix for censored obs
    vector [ntot] t; //time of longitudinal observations
    vector [ntot] y; //outcome of longitudinal observations
    real<lower=0> tcens[ncens]; // time of censorship
    real<lower=0> tuncens[nuncens]; // event time
  vector [npredlong] mublong; // mean of coefficients for longitudinal part (vector 0 as data)
    vector [npredsurv] mubsurv;// mean of coefficients for survival part (vector 0 as data)
}
    
parameters{
    real <lower=0> sigmaeps; // scale for longitudianl part
    vector [npredlong] betalong; // beta for long part
    vector [npredsurv] betasurv; //// beta for surv part
    
  matrix [2,nsubj] raneff; // random effects
  corr_matrix [npredlong] omegalong; //corr matrix for long part coefficients
  corr_matrix [npredsurv] omegasurv; //corr matrix for surv part coefficients
  vector <lower=0> [npredlong] taulong; // noraml vector for long part coefficients
  vector <lower=0> [npredsurv] tausurv;// noraml vector for surv part coefficients

  
    real join0; //joining par
    real join1;//joining par
    real <lower=0> alpha; //weibull shape
    real <lower=1> tcens2 [ncens]; //estimated time for censored
    vector <lower=0> [nraneff] sigraneff; //for defining corr matrix for random effects
    cholesky_factor_corr [nraneff] Lu;  //for defining corr matrix for random effects
}
    
transformed parameters{
    matrix [nraneff,nsubj] uraneff;
    uraneff=diag_pre_multiply(sigraneff,Lu)*raneff;
}
    
model{
    vector [ntot] linpredlong;
    vector [nuncens] linpreduncens;
    vector [ncens] linpredcens;
    vector [ncens] etacens;
    vector [nuncens] etauncens;
    for (i in 1:ntot)
    linpredlong[i]=xlong[i]*betalong+uraneff[1,subj[i]]+uraneff[2,subj[i]]*t[i];
    for (i in 1:nuncens){
    linpreduncens[i]=xuncens[i]*betasurv;
    etauncens[i]=linpreduncens[i]+join0*uraneff[1,subj[i]]+join1*uraneff[2,subj[i]];}
    for (i in 1:ncens){
    linpredcens[i]=xcens[i]*betasurv;
    etacens[i]=linpredcens[i]+join0*uraneff[1,subj[i]]+join1*uraneff[2,subj[i]];}

    join0~normal(0,1);
    join1~normal(0,1);
    alpha~gamma(1,1);
   sigmaeps~gamma(1,1);
    Lu~ lkj_corr_cholesky(2.0);
    to_vector(raneff) ~ normal(0,1);
    taulong~cauchy(0,2.5);
    tausurv~cauchy(0,2.5);
    omegalong~lkj_corr(2);
    omegasurv~lkj_corr(2);

    betalong~multi_normal(mublong,quad_form_diag(omegalong,taulong));
    betasurv~multi_normal(mubsurv,quad_form_diag(omegasurv,tausurv));
    
    y~normal(linpredlong,sigmaeps);
    for (i in 1:nuncens)
    tuncens[i] ~ weibull(alpha, exp(-etauncens[i] / alpha));   //weibull for events
    for (i in 1:ncens)
    tcens2[i] ~ weibull(alpha, exp(-etacens[i] / alpha)/tcens[i]); // weibull for censored
}

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Joint survival-longitudinal model in stan
parts:
You should use a Cholesky factor parameterization of the
correlation matrix and then scale rather than using a full
correlation matrix. But for N = 2 that shouldn't be a problem.

Also, this is almost certainly a bug:

> y~normal(linpredlong,sigmaeps);

Did you mean y[i]? What you're doing is modeling ntot copies of
all of y.

It helps if you indent properly to see the scope of loops.

And if you tell us what you expecte dand what was disappointing.
Otherwise we're just guessing.

- Bob

Thanks Bob. The bug you referred was a copy-paste issue. Actually when I run a model with Cholesky factor things come even worse. 
I use cholesky_factor_corr for random effects and define multivariate normal prior on fixed coefficients by quad_form_diag.
After 30000 iterations, n_eff<5, Rhat>5, many exceptions thrown at weibull scale, and very large coefficient estimates.
I was wondering if there was a problem with code.
Openbugs gives correct output in a few minutes, but I could not define new distribution instead of normal.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Joint survival-longitudinal model in stan
parts:
You want to use the Cholesky-factor parameterization if you
want fast and stable multivariate sampling. But that'll just
make the code faster---it shouldn't change the results.

That code's too long and I'm too unfamiliar with the model to
be able to help debug. Could you recreate the same model as
you coded in BUGS?

You want to make sure to run BUGS from diffuse initialization
points to diagnose convergence.

- Bob
